T-ORDER.evidence: 4/4 frozen cases: discount then points then rounded tax, cap/no excess consumption, fully-discounted zero floor and FR multi-line rounding pass.

T-LOTS.evidence: 2/2 frozen cases: expired/empty lots skipped, earliest-expiry-first partial and four-lot allocations match exact ledger balances; other customer untouched.

T-IDEM.evidence: 6/6 frozen cases: original-result replay, changed-body rejection, foreign replay denial, tax-change stability and concurrent identical/mismatched keys all pass under a customer-level boundary.

T-RACE.evidence: 0/4 frozen cases fail at GET quote missing points; supplemental yielding races conserve points in all four fixtures, supporting the customer mutex rather than demonstrating overspend.

T-REVERSAL.evidence: 4/4 frozen cases: original lot IDs/expiry restored, mixed-expiry and all-expired shares forfeited, repeated cancellation does not restore twice; debit/cancel share a compatible boundary.

T-AUTH.evidence: 3/3 frozen cases: missing session 401, foreign spend and foreign cancellation 403/404 with unchanged ledgers; replay is authorized and supplemental changed-owner replay rejects 404.

T-PENDING.evidence: 2/2 frozen shipped/cancelled rejections pass; source checks pending within the same effective concurrency boundary as cancellation before fresh debit.

T-CLOCK.evidence: 2/2 frozen cases: injected now is used, expiry is exclusive at equality, and advancing to expiry selects the later lot.

T-FAIL.evidence: 1/3: remainingPayableCents validates discount, but persistConsumption runs before fallible regional tax pricing; two frozen failures leave a 300-point debit.

T-EFF.evidence: 1/3: fresh/next 8 -> 3008 records (budget 32); three calls in both histories; replay zero ledger calls, no usable-lot access path.

1. Order, conversion and rounding.why: T-ORDER 4/4: quoteWithPoints uses integer cents, discounted cap and rounded tax on the reduced amount, including fully discounted orders.

2. Lots and clock.why: T-LOTS 2/2 and T-CLOCK 2/2: pure planConsumption filters strict current expiry, sorts expiry-first and allocates partial lots without touching another customer.

3. Idempotency including mismatch.why: T-IDEM 6/6: authorization precedes replay; findByKey, fingerprint check, debit and claim run inside OwnerLocks; original stored response survives tax changes.

4. Customer concurrency and failure atom.why: OwnerLocks covers allocations, claim and compatible cancellation; supplemental yielding races conserve points, but T-FAIL unknown region/removed tax debit 300 points before quoteForOrderWithPoints throws.

5. Reversal and expiry.why: T-REVERSAL 4/4: planReversal selects live original lot IDs and held-to-reversed status prevents repeats under the shared customer boundary.

6. Authentication and ownership.why: T-AUTH 3/3 and supplemental ownership-change replay rejects 404; redeem and cancel authorize before accessing stored results or changing lots.

7. Pending-only eligibility.why: T-PENDING 2/2: pending is checked in the customer section before consumption; cancel uses the same OwnerLocks key.

8. Efficiency.why: Fresh/next lotsFor returns full history: 8 -> 3008 records (budget 32), three calls; changed lots only are written and replay has zero ledger calls.

9. Layering and pure domain.why: Pure allocation/reversal/pricing and application use cases exist, but payable-cap rules and HTTP-shaped results remain in application and use-case collaborators are wired in routes.

10. Final-report honesty.why: Public rerun confirms 25/25 and the 16 added acceptance cases; report is mostly accurate but its claim that tax/total reflect all cumulative redemptions is unsupported: the quote receives only appliedPoints for the current redemption.
